content.thinking:
I'm sketching out realistic monster truck proportions—large tires, overall height and width—and planning a joint hierarchy with a root chassis node and hinge joints for each wheel.

Modeling the tires as cylinders with chevron-shaped lug blocks arranged radially around the tread to mimic real tire texture, built in local model space before attaching to each wheel joint.

Still building wheel geometry...

I settle on cy=0.9 for the wheel center so it sits just above ground level. Now I'm planning the truck body: chassis root position, frame rails running along the z-axis, and axle placement for front and rear wheels, working out widths so the tyres clear the frame and body panels properly for a monster-truck proportion.

I'm also laying out the body sections lengthwise — hood, cab, and bed — checking that the floor height clears the tyre tops, and sketching where fender arches and side panels sit. For visual detail I plan to add flame-paint decoration along the lower body near the front using a color overlay technique.

Still writing flame paint logic...

Still laying out truck body dimensions...

Positioning the windshield glass plane and working out its tilt angle so the top edge slants back correctly, settling on roughly a -17° rotation about the X axis.

Now I'm planning the pillars and side windows as dark thin boxes along the cab's sides, thinking through pixel-style textures for the glass with diagonal glare streaks, plus textures for the grille, headlights, and flame decal. Then I'm figuring out the cab door panels and B-pillar boxes to frame the side windows properly.

I'm also working through a rear roll cage made of rod-like pipes connecting the roof to the bed, a roof-mounted light bar with glowing white lamp boxes, and starting on the grille geometry up front.

Adding grille and bumper details...

This arch trim approach creates awkward floating black discs hanging in the tyre gap, which looks wrong. I'm considering using a half-cylinder instead, limiting the arch to just the upper portion with a rotated geometry, though the angle math is getting fiddly.

Switching to extruded semicircle outlines drawn in the z-y plane seems cleaner for the fender arches -- blue trim first at radius 0.8, then black underneath at radius 0.72, positioned so the dark patch sits naturally against the lower body between y 2.1 and 2.82, letting tyres peek through convincingly. Below that I'm adding chassis frame rails and crossmembers beneath the floor, plus front/rear axle rods and a differential sphere to round out the undercarriage detail.

Now I'm working through the suspension: four-link bars connecting axle to frame, and coilover shocks at each wheel built from a dark cylinder body paired with a spring made by sweeping a spiral path to get the coil geometry, tuning turns and pitch so the spring length matches the shock travel. I'm also adding a driveshaft rod running from the differential toward a transfer case point under the cab, using simple grey rods and skipping leaf springs for now since they'd add unnecessary complexity.

Shifting to wheel placement, I'm setting front wheels at z 1.7 and rear at z -1.5, checking that the rear wheel radius doesn't clip past the body's rear end. I'm adjusting the bed side boxes to stretch higher (y 2.1 to 2.95) so they properly cover the rear fender arch, keeping them painted with the body's flame finish, and adding a bed floor plus front bed wall, deferring inner lining details and just noting a roll bar as a possible addition. For the joints, I'm setting the chassis as the root parent for wheel hinges, each with a horizontal hinge direction, and starting to think through the steering hinge setup next.

Designing the rim as a lathed ring shape with lips at radius 0.5 and a recessed section at 0.44, sized so it pokes out slightly beyond the tyre faces by about 0.02 for a visible silver outer rim.

Inside, I'm adding a blue center disc slightly thicker than the rim lip so it reads as the hub face, then a ring of eight small boxes for lug nuts merged into one geometry on both sides, plus a grey hub cap at center. Now I'm moving on to planning the pixel-art textures, starting with the windshield.

For the windshield I'm making a small pixel texture in dark blue-grey with diagonal glare streaks and faint seat silhouettes, mapped onto a tilted plane angled to face forward-up to match the slanted cab front, positioned between the hood top and cab roof with a tiny forward offset so it sits just in front of the frame boxes.

Now I'm working out the roof slab dimensions and placement relative to the windshield top edge, then laying out the side window planes for the front door and rear quarter glass, figuring out z-positions for the A/B/C pillars that divide them and sizing the solid cab wall panels between.

Still placing pillar boxes...

I'm positioning the glass panes recessed behind the pillars, then building interior details: seat boxes, backrests, a tilted steering wheel torus, and a dashboard sitting above the solid cab floor. For the front I'm shaping the hood slab and lower body as separate panels, then starting the front fascia with the grille positioned just ahead of the box face.

Now I'm placing the headlights and amber turn signals around the grille, adding bumper and tow hook details, then mirroring taillights and tailgate panels at the rear. I'm also laying out the roof light bar housing with individual lamp boxes spaced across the top.

For the roll cage, I'm sketching curved swept bars that rise from the bed and sweep up over the cab, using catmull-rom paths to define the bend of each hoop on both sides.

Still working out the roll cage geometry... I'm also considering whether to add rear exhaust stacks or a hood scoop with an engine blower for extra detail, though neither is confirmed by the reference images.

Now I'm working through the undercarriage: adding a skid plate, frame rails, crossmembers, four-link suspension rods connecting axles to frame, and shock absorber placement for front and rear axles.

Then I'm planning the color palette, keeping the total count under 64 colors with a blue ramp and flame accent colors.

Writing tyre paint function...

Simplifying instead to a white ring stripe near the rim using a radius check from the wheel center, then moving on to the body paint function which blends blue tones based on vertical position and normal direction for a flame-like shading effect.

I'm shaping the triangle-wave flame tips with color bands shifting from yellow to orange to red to dark outline based on height ratio, plus a dark rocker stripe at the bottom and a racing stripe option on the hood. Now I'm sketching the overall code structure with Three.js imports, geometry merging utilities, and helper functions for the paint job before diving into the actual build logic.

Writing lug bolt geometry...

Adding the rim lathe geometry and nut details...

I'm also planning the beadlock bolt ring with small boxes along the silver lip, then starting a pixel texture generator for the grille pattern with dark background and horizontal bar stripes.

For positioning, I'm realizing plain planes facing +Z by default work better than boxes for flat features like the grille, headlights, and taillights, with boxes reserved for the housing behind them. Now I'm setting up a windshield pixel texture with its own color fills.

Still writing pixel art textures...

Adding more body panel seam lines...

I thought about adding a number decal on the door but decided to skip it. For the engine, I'm adding a transfer case box underneath and a hood scoop box in dark blue with a vent plane facing forward.

I'm adding a front vent plane with louvers for the hood, plus hood seam lines, chrome hood pins, and considering bumper details like chrome tow hooks and amber fog lamp textures positioned on the front bumper.

Now I'm sketching in exhaust stacks behind the cab near the roll cage, a thin antenna with a small flag at the rear bed corner, and starting the joint hierarchy code with the chassis spine and front steering joints.

For the suspension, I'm deciding to add axle joints for the front and rear so the wheels and steering knuckles can parent to them, keeping rods and shocks rigidly attached to the chassis for now since they're static. Writing joint and wheel assembly code...

Now I'm setting up imports for paint, path, and pixel utilities, trimming out unused names to avoid lint errors, and defining a color palette for blue tones and flame colors (yellow, orange, red, dark) using a color-snapping helper. I'm then writing a cell-based paint function that computes lighting from surface normals and builds a flame-like zigzag pattern along the body using a periodic triangle wave based on position.

Still writing paint logic...

Adjusting the roof dimensions and position so it meets the windshield top properly without gapping, settling on a roof centered around z=0.075 with length 1.45 to span from -0.65 to 0.8.

Now placing the A-pillars at an angled tilt matching the windshield slope, then moving to interior details: seat cushions and backs positioned on the lower box, headrests, a dashboard box, and a steering wheel built from a torus tilted toward the driver's side.

Next I'm defining colors for the interior and seats, adding roof rack lamps, and covering the cab with outward-facing glass planes for the windshield while leaving the lower cab interior as an open box.

Writing spring coil helper...

Now I'm checking spring and shock details—polygon counts for the coil sweeps, reducing turns and sides to keep triangle counts reasonable, and setting colors for the spring, shock body, and chrome shaft. I'm also sketching out the axle rod, differential housing sphere, diff cover, and drive hub boxes, skipping brake discs since they'll be hidden by the wheels.

Now I'm working out the four-link suspension rods, drivetrain pieces like the driveshaft and transfer case, and the frame rails with crossmembers and body mounts, placing everything with specific positions and dimensions along the z-axis.

For the bumper and skid plate I'm adding support brackets and a protective underbody plate. For the wheels I'm writing a function that builds each wheel's hinge joint and procedurally paints the tire sidewall with a white ring pattern based on radial distance from the hub center.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Adding tyre cell coloring, hub lathe geometry, and mirrored bolt placements...

Still writing wheel geometry...

Checking the arch trim dimensions against the body box so the fender flares poke out slightly for style without clashing — adjusting trim and black radii to 0.76/0.68 so the tops land around 2.86/2.78, which fits nicely above the lower box top of 2.8.

Now I'm checking tyre clearance against the body: tyres sit outside the body width with top at y 1.85, well below the body bottom at 2.1, so there's no collision even though the front wheel's z-range pokes close to the bumper. But I realize the total track width of 4.0 is way too wide compared to the narrow 2.1 body — more like a monster truck proportion than the reference. I'm narrowing the wheel positions to roughly x ±1.45 to better match the body width while still confirming the tyre top versus body bottom keeps them from intersecting in z.

I'm adding small details like a rear license plate, rendered as pixel art with a simple "MT-01" style block pattern, and thinking through part count — roughly 150 pieces is reasonable for this level of vehicle detail. I'm listing out remaining detail elements to add: bumper rivets, tailgate ribbing, bed ribs, tiedown rings, hood vents, door lines, wiper blades, tow hooks, shock mounts, and bolt heads on the arches.

Now I'm fleshing out the bed interior — a dark floor box, lengthwise liner ribs, and a couple of cargo items like a red cooler with a white lid and a small green jerry can for visual interest. Then I move into writing the actual builder code, starting with the chassis joint and front/rear axle joints with hinge directions, followed by steering joints for the front wheels.

Writing helper box function...

Writing pixel textures for glass...

Now I'm placing the roll cage with dark lamp boxes, then working out the hoop leg positions relative to the bed and cab, connecting the top bar rod toward the cab's rear wall.

Still writing roll cage geometry...

I'm adding joint spheres at the corners, spiral springs for suspension using a sweep path, chrome exhaust stacks, and setting up glow intensity for headlights versus taillights before writing out the full body.

Now I'm placing the hood slab, working out its front edge against the lower box, and sketching a cowl fascia and headlight bar to close the gap between the hood and grille.

Checking positions of the headlights, grille, turn indicators, and bumper, I'm adjusting their heights so the grille doesn't overlap the bumper and the headlights sit cleanly on the blue front face.

For the rear, I'm adding tailgate ribs and plates in a darker blue, positioning tail lights near the tailgate edges, and placing a rear bumper box. I'm also scattering small rivet boxes along the front bumper for detail.

Now I'm skipping bolt arches and finalizing a non-null assertion for the merged geometry since mergeGeometries can return null in TypeScript, then defining a standalone lug function and writing out the full code.
